methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Airship Industries is a pre-seed stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The comparable universe consists of 8 private companies operating in the same sector, including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro. No public comps exist in this narrow category.

The peer-median valuation method is not applicable to this analysis. Despite identifying 7 same-sector peers, the pre-seed stage and early development phase of Airship Industries creates insufficient overlap with comparable transactions. The dataset contains zero pre-seed or adjacent-stage transactions and zero similar-tier valuations within the Drones & Autonomous sector. Applying an all-sector median would misrepresent the company's position relative to its true peer set, as the identified private companies operate at materially different stages and scales than a pre-seed entrant.

Without a sufficiently robust comparable set meeting minimum thresholds for stage, valuation tier, and temporal proximity, standard triangulation methods cannot be reliably applied. A defensible valuation of Airship Industries would require additional primary data collection—including investor commitments, detailed financial projections, or transaction precedents from early-stage autonomous systems companies. The key uncertainty remains the absence of pre-seed or seed-stage transaction data within the Drones & Autonomous sector sufficient to establish meaningful valuation benchmarks.
